title: date, time, datetime-local, month, week support considerations
learningObjectives: Explain date, time, datetime-local, month, week support considerations and build forms with appropriate native HTML behaviour.

understand.concept: Date and time input types include date, time, datetime-local, month, and week. Browser interfaces and support details vary, and values use defined machine-readable formats. datetime-local represents a local date and time without a time-zone offset.
understand.whyItMatters: Native controls can differ across browsers and platforms. Applications should validate ranges and business rules on the server, handle locale presentation separately from submitted values, and provide a usable fallback when needed.
understand.analogy: A date picker is a convenient calendar interface, but the stored value follows a standard data format rather than the user's displayed date style.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual form submission and validation follow HTML algorithms and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The browser provides date/time controls where supported. Inspect submitted values and do not assume a time zone is included in datetime-local.

examples.code: <form><label>Date <input type='date' name='date'></label><label>Time <input type='time' name='time'></label><label>Local date and time <input type='datetime-local' name='meeting'></label><label>Month <input type='month' name='month'></label><label>Week <input type='week' name='week'></label></form>
examples.explanation: The browser provides date/time controls where supported. Inspect submitted values and do not assume a time zone is included in datetime-local.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form demonstrating the HTML form behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a booking form with date and time fields. Add min/max constraints and explain why server-side validation is still required.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form using appropriate input types, names, labels, and constraints. Inspect the submitted FormData and explain which controls are successful.
hints: Give every user-facing control a visible label.
Do not trust hidden fields or client-side validation for security.
Test keyboard and mobile input behaviour.

questions.prompt: Does datetime-local include a time-zone offset in its value?
questions.explanation: datetime-local represents a local date and time without a time-zone offset.

questions.prompt: What is a good form-design principle?
options: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.answer: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.explanation: Accessible forms use appropriate controls and labels, while security validation belongs on the server.
